Kai Ryssdal is the host of Marketplace. But he was also once 34 years-old, making $7 an hour at a bookstore in Palo Alto at the height of the dot-com boom. 

In the first episode of Best of Luck, Kyla Scanlon and Kai investigate the biggest turning points of his career for lessons that still apply, and discuss how to connect labor market data to your career decisions. Plus: Kai applies for a new job at Lighthouse Keeper Inc.

00:00 The economy is turning against workers
02:40 Why Kai Ryssdal joined the Navy
04:03 34 making $7
07:18 Takeaway: What do you do for free?
11:03 Can you still bounce around in the modern economy? 
15:18 What labor market data means for your job
18:16 Worst & best career advice
23:25 Advice for every age group & career level
28:57 Kai applies for a new job 
32:02 Luck questionnaire 

Follow Best of Luck on Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/bestofluckpodcast
Follow Kyla Scanlon on Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/kylascan 

Further reading
The Age of Work by Marketplace: https://www.marketplace.org/age-of-work
The Big Money in Today’s Economy Is Going to Capital, Not Labor (WSJ): https://www.wsj.com/economy/jobs/capital-labor-wealth-economy-2fcf6c2f

snippet.description:
At Kirori Mal College, University of Delhi, Sonia Gupta Mam, Head of Mentorship Program at LevelUp IAS, discusses a question many students face: should they enjoy college life first, or begin preparing for UPSC right away?

Drawing from her own experience, she explains why UPSC should be viewed as a possible route towards a larger career goal, rather than the goal itself.

In this session, she discusses:
* Understanding your career goals before choosing UPSC
* Why college students struggle with consistency
* The difference between planning and execution
* How to learn from mentors, teachers and seniors
* Two essential skills: problem-solving and clear expression
* How to begin with the syllabus, graduation subjects and newspapers

The session is for college students exploring UPSC CSE, including those who are not yet sure whether civil services is the right career choice.
